concept.name: Narrative bias
concept.definition: The tendency to impose coherent stories on sequences of events and to treat a plausible narrative as explanation or evidence, even when outcomes were driven substantially by chance. Taleb calls this the narrative fallacy: we compress complex, random reality into memorable stories and then overtrust them.
concept.intuition: The market rallies and someone supplies a reason; the reason feels like knowledge, but the same story machine would have explained a sell-off just as smoothly.
concept.mechanics: Stories reduce dimensionality and aid memory, so causally tidy accounts crowd out base rates, randomness, and alternative explanations; post-hoc narratives about past moves are then projected forward as if they had predictive force. In trading it corrupts both real-time judgment and post-trade review.
concept.failure_modes: It misleads most in noisy, low-signal domains such as short-term price moves, where a compelling story can be constructed for any outcome. It also makes review unfalsifiable, since every result can be retrofitted with a satisfying cause.
concept.misconceptions: Not all narratives are false - the bias is mistaking a story's coherence for evidence of its truth and underestimating the role of luck. Narratives are indispensable for communication; the error is treating them as analysis.
concept.example: A trader explains yesterday's rally as rotation into quality on rate expectations; when the market falls the next day, the same factors are cited to explain the drop.
